Author: @karolusmagnus3992
Content:
Great video!
Just to put my two cents in about ASD,
Autism is not a disease and therefore does not have a cure.
Anyone discussing a "cure" for autism is likely not autistic themselves and doesn't have a firm grasp on the disorder as a whole, especially scientifically. Usually it's someone who has a family member with ASD they resent for having too high support needs for them to cope with. (Autism Moms is the big one) In order to "cure" autism we just need to fundamentally restructure society to help neurodivergent and other disabled people have an easier time in the world rather than it being a one size fits all system. (Accessibility and accommodations)
If you want to experience what it's like to be disabled, try doing your normal everyday life with a few restrictions. You can't go on steep inclines or stairs (wheelchair accessible) You can't get your hands wet or dirty at all (a common sensory issue with ASD people) and for extra fun try not being able to speak, and for extra fun in the US pretend you can't drive for a week (Another common trait of ASD individuals). See how easily you fit into the world like that, and then realize there are people who have that as their daily reality. This is why we need accessibility for disabled people.
obviously it would be very hard and expensive to accommodate the small fraction of disabled people, which of course is why we don't do it. I think it's worth spending some of our tremendous collective wealth in modern society to help the disabled, but obviously most people don't agree so I guess I'm the weird one on this.

Thank you for coming to my TED talk!

Content: BR: Orbs have plagued ghost-hunting for decades. They are one of the most common types of photographic evidence for ghosts. I’ve seen hundreds and hundreds of orb photos. The expectation is what you see in a photograph matches what you saw with your eyes. In the case of orb photographs, the mysterious orbs show up in the photographs after they are developed or are saved to a disk. Typically, the explanation for an orb is a flash reflection. That’s why you don’t see it with your eyes. There will often be some small element like dust, a bug or raindrops, or simply any reflective surface, which reflects the flash.
